name: filler-gru-r3
task: filled-pause (um/uh/er, Hindi aa/umm) per-frame detection on the product front-end
operatingPoint: max VAL recall at VAL precision >= 0.82 (pre-registered), chosen on val only; test read once
trainingData: AMI Meeting Corpus individual headsets (University of Edinburgh et al.), CC BY 4.0: 84 speakers / 32.7 h (warm start from filler-gru/1, itself AMI CC BY 4.0); FLEURS hi_in + en_us TRAIN read speech (Google), CC BY 4.0, as non-filler negatives. Commercial use permitted with attribution.
notCovered: child speech (no licence-clean child corpus marks fillers; HiACC fire rates only, evaluation only)
Hindi or Hinglish spontaneous fillers as POSITIVES (Hindi appears only as read-speech negatives)
bt / speakerphone routes (narrowband: unusable, the head and the hold cue ignore them)

test.set: AMI 8 Indian-L1 series, 32 held-out speakers (the 2026-10-04 harness)

holdCue.measured: LiveKit EOT-Bench Hindi (CC BY 4.0, 400 ADULT turns): P(hold | fired) 1 (Wilson 95% [0.741, 1]), fired 11, at turn ends 0/400; pComplete = 1 - the lower bound

attribution: Contains information from the AMI Meeting Corpus (University of Edinburgh, IDIAP, TNO et al.), licensed CC BY 4.0, and from FLEURS (Google), licensed CC BY 4.0.
